takeaway: Restrictive disease such as pulmonary fibrosis makes the lungs stiff and reduces the functional residual capacity; obstructive disease increases it.

question.text: What causes a reduction in pulmonary functional residual capacity?
question.say: What causes a reduction in pulmonary functional residual capacity?

lines.text: FRC: the air left after a passive breath out.
lines.say: Functional residual capacity is the air left in the lungs at the end of passive expiration. Here it is this little jar.

lines.text: These lungs have turned to stiff wood.
lines.say: (sigh) These lungs have turned to wood. That is pulmonary fibrosis.
Fibrosis makes the lungs stiff and less compliant, like this tight spring.
Stiff lungs hold less air at rest, so the F R C is reduced.

lines.text: Emphysema, bronchitis and asthma raise the FRC.
lines.say: Obstructive diseases, like emphysema, chronic bronchitis and asthma, do the opposite. Air trapping and higher compliance increase the F R C.

lines.text: Remember: restrictive disease like pulmonary fibrosis reduces the FRC.
lines.say: Remember: restrictive disease, like pulmonary fibrosis, reduces the functional residual capacity.
